# Management of Change: A Practical Guide

A change can bring hazards that the original risk assessment never covered. Keep records for 30 years [VERIFY].

## What counts as a change {#what-counts}

- New chemicals or suppliers
- Altered **process conditions**, *new equipment* or ++temporary bypasses++
- ~~Like-for-like replacements~~ (these don't count)

1. Describe the change.
2. Review the hazards.
3. Approve and record it.

## Who signs off

See the [OSHA PSM standard](https://www.osha.gov/process-safety-management), our [SDS page](wagtail://page?id=3), the [MOC template](wagtail://document?id=7) and [what counts](#what-counts). Questions: [email us](mailto:safety@example.com) or [call](tel:+441234567890).

![Engineer reviewing a change request at a control panel](wagtail://image?id=42 "Every change needs a named reviewer.")

![Management of change explained](wagtail://media?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dabc123)

| Change type | Review by |
|---|---|
| Chemical | EHS manager |
| Equipment | Engineering |

:::faq
### Does a temporary change need MOC?

Yes. Temporary changes need the same review and an end date.

### Who keeps the records?

The site EHS manager, for the life of the process.
:::
